panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Caption explicitly attributes perioral eruption to chloracne in Yusho disease; image shows comedonal acneiform eruption in facial distribution matching vocabulary and in-text 'acne-like eruption with comedones, cysts, and pustules'. B: Caption explicitly states 'Scars and cysts from chloracne in the axilla'; real patient clinical photo shows axillary cysts/scars. No axillary finding_key exists in vocabulary, so recorded as proposed_findings. C: Caption explicitly states 'Severe crateriform, or punched-out scars, from chloracne on the back' with ongoing 'Inflammatory acneiform eruption' arrowed; real patient photo matches. No back/scar finding_key in vocabulary, so recorded as proposed_findings.

panels.figure_caption: Clinical features of chloracne in patients with Yusho disease, an outbreak that occurred in Japan in 1968. (A) Chloracne in the perioral area in 1968. (B) Scars and cysts from chloracne in the axilla in 2008. (C) Severe crateriform, or punched-out scars, from chloracne on the back in 2008. Inflammatory acneiform eruption still appears frequently (arrow).
in_text_mentions: Chloracne is characterized by an acne-like eruption with comedones, cysts, and pustules that occurs after exposure to high concentrations of environmental AHR ligands, such as TCDD and PCDF [9,10,11,12,14] (Figure 1; see also [71]). In the Seveso explosion accident, chloracne was also found in children exposed to contaminated air containing high concentrations of TCDD [72].

plate_findings.evidence: caption: 'hyperpigmentation, multiple cysts, chloracne-like lesions of face and neck'

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (a, b, c). a: Clinical photograph of worker B's face and neck showing hyperpigmentation and multiple cysts described as chloracne-like lesions; facial cysts in chloracne distribution directly match the configured disease and the chloracne_facial_cysts vocabulary key. b: Clinical photograph of worker B's trunk showing soft cysts with yellowish pus and papules with comedones (arrow marks biopsy site); truncal distribution is a recognized less common form of chloracne. No vocabulary key covers truncal lesions, so visible manifestations are recorded as proposed findings. c: H&E histopathology of worker B's skin biopsy showing epidermal cysts, hyperkeratosis, chronic granulomatous inflammation and dense fibrosis, consistent with chloracne; the in-text mention of epidermal cysts supports the comedonal cyst histology finding key.

panels.figure_caption: Skin lesions and histopathology of worker B. a. hyperpigmentation, multiple cysts, chloracne-like lesions of face and neck, b. soft cysts with yellowish pus and papules with comedones (arrow: biopsy site), c. Histopathologic findings showed chronic inflammation with dense fibrosis, chronic granulomatous inflammation, hyperkeratosis (hematoxylin and eosin stain, × 40)
in_text_mentions: he findings indicated epidermal cysts, hyperkeratosis, increased basal pigmentation, chronic perivascular inflammation, chronic granulomatous inflammation, and pigmented macrophages in dermis (Figure 1). Injection therapy was performed to treat the keloid scar that developed in the chest area, and both punch biopsy and squeezing were performed to treat the cysts.
